designNarrative: ArchiveRecords gains a root parameter and applies a byte-level substring strip (root+separator) to the copied run-state.json, run-events.jsonl, and typed state/*.json before writing them into the committed feature archive, leaving the workspace's own absolute-path copies untouched. root is resolved independently inside recordEpisode via filepath.Abs("."), the same expression run.go's prepareRunWorkspace already uses, which keeps the whole diff inside internal/memory/** and cmd/loom/cmd/run_memory.go without threading a new parameter through run.go. The change is a narrow adapter-layer fix — two small unexported helpers, no new dependency edges, no schema change. Behaviour change: yes.
securitySurface: No new trust boundary: this rewrites files loom itself already wrote to its own workspace/archive directories. No user-controlled input reaches the strip beyond the repository's own absolute path.
performanceSurface: Full-file bytes.ReplaceAll per copied file (run-state.json, run-events.jsonl, state/*.json) — bounded by one run's artifact sizes, no loop over unbounded external data.
testDesignReview: TestArchiveRelativizesPathsUnderRoot: YES — loads the archived run-state.json and asserts Stages["analyst"].ArtifactPath equals the expected relative path; fails if stripping regresses.
TestArchivePreservesAPathOutsideRoot: YES — asserts SpecPath stays byte-identical to the out-of-root value; fails if the strip over-matches.

TestArchiveStripsRootFromEventText: YES — asserts the archived event's Error no longer contains root but still contains 'permission denied', and that every line still unmarshals; fails if stripping corrupts JSON or misses the text.

TestArchivedRecordsNeverContainTheRoot: YES — asserts !bytes.Contains(root) across run-state.json, run-events.jsonl and every state/*.json file; fails if any archived file leaks the absolute path. Note: the typed-state fixture content (writeTypedState) never contained root to begin with, so this assertion holds for state/*.json 'by construction' rather than by observed stripping — a gap already named and accepted in analysis.md's Edge Cases section, not a new issue.

TestArchiveLeavesTheWorkspaceByteIdentical: YES — reads the workspace's own run-state.json/run-events.jsonl before and after ArchiveRecords and asserts byte equality; fails if copyRelativized ever wrote back to the source.

Seven pre-existing tests (TestArchiveRecordsCopiesBothFiles, TestArchiveKeepsTheTypedStageDocuments, TestArchiveSkipsARejectedPayload, TestArchiveToleratesNoTypedState, TestArchiveToleratesAMissingTimeline, TestArchiveKeepsTheMarkdownArtifacts, TestArchiveLeavesNonArtifactsBehind): YES, unchanged — only a mechanical third "" argument was added; their original assertions are untouched and still would fail under the same regressions they always caught.
selfReviewCheck: Complexity < 7 claim: verified true — golangci-lint run (gocyclo min-complexity 7) reports 0 issues against the changed files.
No boolean parameter added: verified true — copyRelativized is a new sibling function, not a flag on copyIfPresent.

'No new import added to internal/memory/workspace.go' (implementation-notes.md Self-Review Checklist, and architecture-notes.md's Layer Boundary Check PASS rationale): FALSE. git show HEAD:internal/memory/workspace.go confirms "bytes" was not previously imported; the diff adds it. The PASS verdict itself still holds — bytes is standard library, so no new dependency edge outside the permitted set was actually introduced — but the stated evidence for that verdict is inaccurate. Flagged per the discrepancy-is-a-finding instruction; non-blocking because the underlying architectural claim (no new internal/external dependency edge) remains true despite the wrong supporting detail.
'git diff touches only internal/memory/**, cmd/loom/cmd/run_memory.go, and docs/features/delivery-record-relative-paths/' claim: verified true via git status --short.
'cmd/loom/cmd/run.go is unchanged' claim: verified true via git diff; and filepath.Abs(".") at run.go:290 is confirmed identical to the expression now duplicated in recordEpisode.
